name: Calibration can remove a failing confidence term
non_visual_rationale: A named term inside an operator-only file; no user surface carries confidence changes until the scoring lane acts.
criteria_delivered: 1. src/learning/metrics.ts's calibrationOf bins each captured report by its own predicted.conf_level (read permissively off the row, same as before), against quality in {good, epic} as the hit and score_q/100 as the naive v1 probability. calibration.bins is now an array of {conf_level, reports, hits, hit_rate, brier} rows sorted by conf_level (previously a Record<string,{...}> keyed by conf_level, with the same four fields but no conf_level field on the row itself) -- the shape the AT's own oracle (support/monthly-port.ts's metricAt + binFor) requires and 06 section 10's stated bin shape names.

2. calibrationOf gains offendingTermOf(bins): compares the 'high' and 'low' bins' hit rates and names 'c_spread' only on a STRICT inversion (high.hit_rate < low.hit_rate); a tie or a non-inversion names null. AT scenario 1 (30 alternating mornings, every confident morning bad, every hesitant one good) proves high.hit_rate=0 < low.hit_rate=1 names 'c_spread'; AT scenario 2 (confidenceWasRight=true, the control) proves the non-inverted month names null. Both scenarios pass at GREEN.

3. offending_term is a name, not an action: calibrationOf performs no store write and evaluate.ts needed no change at all -- runMonthlyEvaluationOnce already threads buildMonthlyMetrics straight into the one file it writes under learned/metrics/v1/, and the AT's own assertWritesConfinedToMetrics harness (which every slice-05 AT runs) confirms the run still writes exactly one file, only under that prefix. The scoring lane's own edit (deleting C_spread from src/scoring/engine.ts) is explicitly out of this step's owned paths and was not touched.
criteria_deferred: A three-way comparison including the 'medium' confidence level is not built. The design context and the AT fixture both name only 'high' and 'low' as the compared pair (09 section 3.6 consequence 3's own framing); a future step wanting a 'medium' role in the kill switch needs its own criterion and its own AT evidence.

The scoring lane's removal of C_spread itself (src/scoring/engine.ts) is explicitly routed, not performed, per the roadmap criterion 3 and design context. This step ships only the naming; a later slice or a different lane owns the deletion.
scope_note: files_to_modify named src/learning/evaluate.ts as a candidate; it needed no edit. runMonthlyEvaluationOnce already calls buildMonthlyMetrics and writes its full return value verbatim to the one metrics file, so calibration.offending_term reaches the file the moment metrics.ts computes it -- no separate wiring existed to add. This mirrors 05-03's scope_note precedent (cross-validation.ts needed no change either) and is confirmed by the post-GREEN wiring check below: git diff --name-only shows only metrics.ts changed in src/, and every falsifiability mutation below was planted and caught inside that one file.
design_decisions_not_stated_upstream: calibration.bins changed shape from Record<string, {reports,hits,hit_rate,brier}> (05-01's shipped form) to an array of {conf_level, reports, hits, hit_rate, brier} rows. Grepped src/ and tests/ for '.bins' before making the change: the only consumer anywhere in the tree was this step's own new AT (support/monthly-port.ts's binFor requires Array.isArray(bins) and a conf_level field per row). The sealed 05-01 AT (the-monthly-file-watches-every-hazard-the-design-names.test.ts) only asserts calibration is a truthy object, never inspects .bins' shape, so it stayed green unedited. typecheck and the full suite both confirm no other breakage.

offendingTermOf compares only the literal 'high' and 'low' conf_level tokens (ConfLevel is 'low'|'medium'|'high' elsewhere in the codebase, src/publish/static-surface.ts). A 'medium' bin, if present, plays no role in the comparison -- neither promoted nor excluded from the bins array, just not part of the two-sided check. This is the design context's own framing ('compares only the high and low confidence bins the fixture defines') rather than an invented three-way rule.

A tie (high.hit_rate === low.hit_rate) is read as non-inverted and names null, not 'c_spread' -- only a STRICT inversion fires. Neither AT scenario constructs an exact tie, so this is a design decision extrapolated from '(high strictly less often right than low)' in the roadmap criterion text, pinned instead by the unit equivalence-law property, which exercises exact ties whenever fast-check happens to generate identical hit rates on both sides.
acceptance: a-confidence-level-that-does-not-predict-correctness-is-named.test.ts, pre-authored by DISTILL, describe.skip removed (the only touch made to the file). Two scenarios: (1) a 30-morning alternating month where every confident morning was bad and every hesitant one good must name calibration.offending_term 'c_spread', with both bins carrying their 15-report count, hit counts (0 and 15), hit rates (0 and 1) and a numeric brier; (2) the control month (confidence predicted correctly) must name null. Both scenarios pass at GREEN; no oracle was edited.
unit_law: Three fast-check properties appended to tests/unit/learning-metrics.test.ts, none of which the AT's two fixed examples can prove alone: (1) 'the equivalence law' -- offending_term equals 'c_spread' exactly when both a high and a low bin exist and high.hit_rate is strictly lower, null otherwise, over arbitrary generated logs including the branch no AT fixture ever produces (one or both bins entirely absent) -- this generalizes roadmap criterion 2 beyond the two fixed months and directly encodes 'absence must never manufacture a removal'; (2) 'correctness against an independently computed oracle' -- a Modeling-strategy reference (Hebert ch.3, the same shape as the file's existing mae.per_key-vs-hEff oracle) independently aggregates reports/hits/hit_rate/brier per conf_level from the generated rows and asserts the production bins match exactly, plus the standing brier in [0,1] bound; (3) 'order-independence' -- permuting the observation array (fc.shuffledSubarray at full length) yields identical bins (per-field, with a small floating-point tolerance on hit_rate/brier for summation-order-only differences) and an identical offending_term.
test_budget: 4 distinct behaviors this step touches: (a) bins reshaped to an array with conf_level, computed correctly per an independent oracle; (b) offending_term equivalence law, generalized (inversion names c_spread, non-inversion or a missing side names null); (c) order-independence of the bin aggregation; (d) the routed-not-performed no-write guarantee, already covered by every slice-05 AT's shared assertWritesConfinedToMetrics harness, not a new behavior this step introduces. Budget = 2 x 3 new behaviors (a,b,c) = 6. This step authored 3 new unit properties (one per behavior) plus activated 2 pre-authored AT scenarios (DISTILL-authored, covering (b)'s two concrete instances). Total new+activated test count = 5, within budget; no consolidation pattern needed.

falsifiability_evidence: Four mutations to src/learning/metrics.ts, each reverted and diff-confirmed clean via `git diff --stat` and a full green re-run. (1) Inverted the comparison from `high.hit_rate < low.hit_rate` to `>`: re-ran the AT + unit file -> EXIT=1, 3 failed -- both AT scenarios (inversion now names null, control now names 'c_spread') and the equivalence-law property. (2) Removed the missing-bin guard, defaulting absent sides to 0/1 (`(high?.hit_rate ?? 0) < (low?.hit_rate ?? 1)`): re-ran -> EXIT=1, 1 failed -- only the equivalence-law property caught it ('bins=[]' -- an empty-log case manufactured 'c_spread' from nothing); both AT scenarios stayed green because neither ever produces a missing bin, which is exactly why the unit law earns its place. (3) Set `brier: 0` unconditionally: re-ran -> EXIT=1, 1 failed -- the independent-oracle property caught the wrong number ('brier must equal the independently computed mean squared error ... {"brier":0}'); this mutation was planted specifically because a prior draft of the arithmetic property (bounds-only, brier in [0,1]) let `brier:0` through silently -- the oracle property replaced it before commit. (4) Removed the `.sort(([left],[right]) => left.localeCompare(right))` call feeding bins: re-ran -> EXIT=1, 1 failed on the first generated case -- the order-independence property caught bins landing in Map-insertion order instead of a stable conf_level order under a shuffle ('bins must land in the same conf_level order'). All four reverted; the committed diff (verified via `git show --numstat HEAD`) is metrics.ts +36/-19 lines (the calibration section), the AT skip-marker +1/-1 line, and the unit test file +138/-0 lines, and a full-suite green re-run followed each revert.
